brand.legal: Jaden Green, doing business as GreenAI Solutions

niche.headline: Three AI employees, built for one trade: pool service.
niche.one_line: GreenAI builds, trains and runs three AI employees for residential pool service companies in the Phoenix metro — each one custom-made for your company, your prices and your routes.
niche.buyer: Owner of a residential weekly pool service company (1–10 trucks) in Phoenix / Mesa / Gilbert / Chandler / Scottsdale / Tempe / Glendale / Peoria that also does repairs.
why_this_niche: Flat recurring revenue: weekly service runs $110–$150/month per pool (verified from local companies' own sites), and customers stay for years.
Phoenix has 257,983 residential pools inside city limits alone — 27.6% of properties (Vexcel aerial survey, the only figure that traces to a primary source).
The owner answers his own phone from a truck. Nobody sets automation up for him — every tool in this trade is do-it-yourself.
Selling window is February–April: owners have route capacity right before the spring rush.
rejected_alternatives: Every Phoenix service business (too broad — the last 18 months of the site).
Pool builders / remodelers ($50k+ jobs, months-long sales cycles, a handful of leads a year — an AI employee has nothing to answer all day).
Pool repair-only specialists (real, but most repair work in Phoenix is done by service companies — this niche already includes them).
Pool supply / retail stores (walk-in traffic and water testing — different systems entirely).
Commercial / HOA pool management (contracts, compliance logs, very few buyers, long procurement).
banned_stats: any customer count, testimonial, logo, ROI %, or 'clients see X'

agents.name: NET
agents.tagline: Every lead answered in 8 seconds. Quoted from your price list. Chased until it books.
channels: Phone (answers, or texts back a missed call)
jobs: Answers a new lead in 8 seconds, any hour, any channel.
Asks the four things a pool quote needs: address, pool size, current condition (green? equipment issues?), and how often they want service.
Quotes weekly and bi-weekly service only from your approved price list — a price that is not on your list is blocked before it sends.
Follows up on day 1, day 3 and day 7 until the lead books or says stop.
Books the first visit into the slot you give it and texts you the address.
Stops the moment someone says stop, and tells you it did.
wont: Never invents a price. If the answer is not on your list, it says the owner will confirm.
Never claims to be a person.
Does not promise a booking count. It promises the reply and the follow-up.
trained_on: Your weekly / bi-weekly prices by pool size
Your name and how you like to be introduced

human_comparison.label: a full-time office person, Phoenix wage + payroll tax

agents.name: BALANCE
agents.tagline: Answers your customers, sends the service note, asks for the review. You stay on the route.
jobs: Answers 'is my tech coming today?', 'why is my pool cloudy?', 'can you skip next week?' from the schedule and house rules you give it.
Sends the after-visit service note (what was done, readings you entered, what to watch) the same day.
Asks for a Google review two days after a visit went well — and routes a complaint to you instead of to Google.
Sends seasonal notices you approve: filter clean due, monsoon debris pass, salt-cell inspection, winter schedule change.
Handles reschedules and gate/dog/access notes and puts them in front of you before the route.
Flags a customer who has gone quiet or complained twice so you can call them before they cancel.
wont: Does not diagnose equipment or give chemical dosing over text — it books a tech visit.
Does not send anything a customer has not agreed to receive; one 'stop' ends all messages.
Never posts a review or writes one — it only asks the customer to.
trained_on: Your weekly route schedule (a sheet or export is enough)
Your house rules: skips, credits, gate access, dogs
What you want said about green pools, algae, monsoon, filter cleans
Which complaints go straight to your phone

human_comparison.label: a part-time customer-service hire, Phoenix wage + payroll tax

agents.name: PUMP
agents.tagline: Open repair quotes chased. Invoices sent. Late payers reminded. Politely, every time.
jobs: Chases every open repair quote (pump, filter, heater, salt cell, leak) on day 2, day 5 and day 10 until it is approved or declined.
Sends the monthly service invoice on the day you pick, with your payment link.
Reminds late payers at 7, 14 and 21 days in the tone you approve — firm, never rude.
Tells you who is 30+ days out so you decide whether to pause service.
Sends the 'we noticed on today's visit' upsell you approve (filter clean, cartridge replacement, acid wash) with your price.
Keeps a Monday list: quotes approved, invoices paid, who still owes.
wont: Never changes a price, offers a discount, or waives a fee on its own.
Never threatens, mentions collections agencies or credit, or contacts anyone but the account holder.
Does not process payments itself — it sends the link to the processor you already use.
trained_on: Your repair price list and quote format
Your invoice day and payment link
Your late-payment policy and pause rule
Your approved upsell list with prices
Your voice: how firm, how friendly

human_comparison.label: a part-time bookkeeper / office assistant, Phoenix wage + payroll tax

terms.billing: Month to month. Cancel any time. You own every script, transcript and configuration.
terms.setup: Built and trained for your company before it goes live; you approve every script first. Unlimited same-day changes.

proof.engine: The same lead engine every agent runs on has a public test drive: 4 leads, 5 quotes, 1 held for approval, 0 messages to an unsubscribed address — and when the model wrote a price as 'custom', the price checker blocked it because it was not on the list.
